import pyomo.environ as pyo

DATA = {
    "nodes": [0, 1, 2, 3, 4],
    "num_selected": 2,
    "scale": 1000000,
    # ordered-pair distances (units), scaled by 1e6
    "dist": {
        (0, 1): 19, (0, 2): 21, (0, 3): 31, (0, 4): 35,
        (1, 0): 29, (1, 2): 13, (1, 3): 46, (1, 4): 37,
        (2, 0): 50, (2, 1): 22, (2, 3): 49, (2, 4): 33,
        (3, 0): 18, (3, 1): 20, (3, 2): 46, (3, 4): 33,
        (4, 0): 18, (4, 1): 26, (4, 2): 39, (4, 3): 43,
    },
    "big_M": 50000000,
}

GOLD_ANSWER = None


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    nodes = d["nodes"]
    scale = d["scale"]
    big_M = d["big_M"]

    # scaled distance lookup
    dist = {(i, j): d["dist"][(i, j)] * scale for (i, j) in d["dist"]}

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # ordered pairs (i,j), i != j
    model.Pairs = pyo.Set(
        initialize=[(i, j) for i in nodes for j in nodes if i != j],
        dimen=2,
    )

    # "Each location can either be selected (1) or not selected (0)."
    model.select = pyo.Var(nodes, within=pyo.Binary)

    # "For every pair of locations, determine whether both are selected as facilities,
    #  represented by a binary decision variable."
    model.pair = pyo.Var(model.Pairs, within=pyo.Binary)

    # "maximize the minimum distance between any two selected facilities"
    # assumption: NonNegativeReals with no upper bound
    model.min_dist = pyo.Var(within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # "The total number of selected facilities must equal two."
    def total_rule(m):
        return sum(m.select[i] for i in nodes) == d["num_selected"]
    model.total_selected = pyo.Constraint(rule=total_rule)

    # "the selection of both facilities in the pair is only possible if both individual
    #  facilities are selected, enforced through constraints linking the pairwise
    #  selection variables to the individual facility selection variables."
    # Upper links: pair[i,j] <= select[i], pair[i,j] <= select[j]
    def pair_upper_i_rule(m, i, j):
        return m.pair[i, j] <= m.select[i]
    model.pair_upper_i = pyo.Constraint(model.Pairs, rule=pair_upper_i_rule)

    def pair_upper_j_rule(m, i, j):
        return m.pair[i, j] <= m.select[j]
    model.pair_upper_j = pyo.Constraint(model.Pairs, rule=pair_upper_j_rule)

    # assumption: forcing lower link pair[i,j] >= select[i] + select[j] - 1
    def pair_lower_rule(m, i, j):
        return m.pair[i, j] >= m.select[i] + m.select[j] - 1
    model.pair_lower = pyo.Constraint(model.Pairs, rule=pair_lower_rule)

    # min_dist <= d[i,j] + big_M * (1 - pair[i,j])
    # assumption: big_M = d_max = 50000000
    def min_dist_link_rule(m, i, j):
        return m.min_dist <= dist[(i, j)] + big_M * (1 - m.pair[i, j])
    model.min_dist_link = pyo.Constraint(model.Pairs, rule=min_dist_link_rule)

    # "The objective is to maximize the minimum distance between any two selected facilities"
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=model.min_dist, sense=pyo.maximize)

    return model
